  "title": "Checkbox to accept Terms",
  "body": "Currently on the auth UI, there is only the phrase \"by continuing you accept...\" the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy. Although this sentence has legal value in most countries of the world, it is not the case everywhere.\r\n\r\nTake the case of French jurisdiction. It considers the general conditions of use as a contract between the publisher and the Internet user. However, this jurisdiction considers a contract valid if only the two parties exchange consents. \r\n\r\n> Le contrat est consensuel lorsqu'il se forme par le seul échange des consentements quel qu'en soit le mode d'expression. [Code civil - Article 1109](https://www.legifrance.gouv.fr/affichCodeArticle.do?idArticle=LEGIARTI000006436120&cidTexte=LEGITEXT000006070721)\r\n\r\nThis implies that the user must accept the general terms of use explicitly (to be considered as a consent) and not implicitly as does the phrase \"by continuing you accept\".\r\nIt is therefore necessary to set up a checkbox, **not pre-checked**, with the sentence \"by checking this box, I acknowledge that I have read...\".\r\n\r\nAs it depends of the country jurisdiction, it could be interesting having one additional parameter as : \r\n``` Java\r\nAuthUI.getInstance()\r\n        .createSignInIntentBuilder()\r\n        .setAvailableProviders(providers)\r\n        .showCheckboxTerms(boolean)\r\n        .build(),\r\n    RC_SIGN_IN);\r\n```",
  "author": "Participant 1",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "@baudev thanks for raising this, I apologize for the slow response but I was gathering some opinions internally.\r\n\r\nFirst of all, we do believe that our current ToS/PP implementation is sufficient.  I am not a lawyer so I won't attempt to explain the rationale.\r\n\r\nThat said, we do we want to support FirebaseUI in a way that's useful for you!  So we are happy to consider this feature for a future release.  It will just require a small API/UI change (as you showed) and  some new string translations for the updates.  I will put this on the schedule for `4.2.0` for now and we'll see how that goes."
    },
    {
      "id": 398276676,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-398276676",
      "created_at": "2018-06-19T05:15:16Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "I think this is pretty important feature. As in some parts of the world, companies are obligated to have user's agreement first.\r\n\r\nHaving a simple checkbox to agree or no will be very useful for them.\r\n\r\nI'd like to try work on it. :)"
    },
    {

      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-399609274",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "@iamyaoxi if you're serious about working on it we'll happily take the contribution!  The only thing we need to do first is agree on the API for turning this on/off and then the rest is implementation."
    },
    {
      "id": 399613945,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-399613945",

      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "@samtstern Ya sure! My idea is similar like that of @baudev \r\n\r\n- Developers can choose if they have ToS and/or PP\r\n- Developers can choose if they want to have checkbox or not.\r\n\r\nIf they have ToS / PP, they go with current implementation. \"By continuing, you are indicating...\".\r\nBut if they have checkbox enabled, a checkbox will appear and the text might change into: \"I have read and accept...\"\r\n\r\nI'm still new in contributing to big open source project like this, but I do want to try. (FYI, I already read and do CONTRIBUTING.md) Would you mind to help me out? Like when you said is to agree with API. Do I make pull request for the API that I suggested and then we go work on the implementation?"
    },

My idea is similar\n> like that of @baudev <https://github.com/baudev>\n>\n>    - Developers can choose if they have ToS and/or PP\n>    - Developers can choose if they want to have checkbox or not.\n>\n> If they have ToS / PP, they go with current implementation. \"By\n> continuing, you are indicating...\".\n> But if they have checkbox enabled, a checkbox will appear and the text\n> might change into: \"I have read and accept...\"\n>\n> I'm still new in contributing to big open source project like this, but I\n> do want to try.       "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-399657486",

      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "Excuse me for not helping you but I don't have time to contribute on this issue.\r\n\r\n> Developers can choose if they want to have checkbox or not.\r\n\r\nEven if it's seems obvious, I just want to insist on the fact that the checkbox **mustn't be pre-checked**. It's a small detail but required by some jurisdiction.\r\n\r\nOtherwise, your API is perfect according to me.\r\nThanks again for working on it 😉 "

    {
      "id": 400087504,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-400087504",
      "created_at": "2018-06-25T20:38:25Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "@baudev agree, no pre-checked boxes.\r\n\r\n@iamyaoxi thanks for the API proposal!  I left a comment there.  Our `CONTRIBUTING.md` file is pretty useless so I'll tell you the basic steps:\r\n\r\n1) Fork the repo\r\n2) Create a new branch based on the current development branch (right now `version-4.1.0-dev`)\r\n3) Implement your feature, try and match the code style of existing code when you can\r\n4) Send us a PR!\r\n\r\nDon't worry if your PR is not perfect on the first try, we will help you get it merged.  This is an important but relatively simple feature so I am confident you will be able to do it without having to understand our whole codebase."
    },
    {
      "id": 400892148,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-400892148",
      "created_at": "2018-06-28T02:36:30Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 3",
      "body": "Hi @samtstern @baudev \r\n\r\nI'd like to ask your idea for this checkbox agreement. Where do you think it will be best to put this explicit acceptance. One of them, for sure, is when Users are registering themselves using email.\r\n\r\nBut I notice that in FirebaseUI flows, Users are not required to register when trying to sign using Social Media or Phone Number. What do you think? Does it mean we need to require their explicit acceptance every time they sign in?"
    },
    {
      "id": 401089375,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-401089375",
      "created_at": "2018-06-28T16:12:12Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 2",
      "body": "(cc @bojeil-google @SUPERCILEX )\r\n\r\nThat's a good question!  I guess I had not thought it through all the way.  When we added the extended ToS/PP on more screens recently we focused on putting it at each entry point:\r\n\r\n- The `AuthMethodPickerActivity` screen\r\n- The start of the email/password flow\r\n  - For new users\r\n  - For existing users\r\n- The start of the phone flow\r\n\r\nYou're right that if you have exactly one provider configured and that provider is \"social\", then you never see the ToS/PP.  For developers with that configuration our recommendation is to get acceptance in your own UI before launching into FirebaseUI since there's no screen for us to put it on.\r\n\r\nSo for \"explicit acceptance\" we have a few options:\r\n  1. Put it everywhere that we put the \"extended\" ToS/PP right now.\r\n  2. Only put it on the `AuthMethodPickerActivity` screen\r\n\r\nWe could make (2) work for everyone if we force the `AuthMethodPickerActivity` screen to be shown for one-provider configurations if you require explicit acceptance (rather than skipping it as we do now).  I think it's a lot simpler than (1) which has a lot of cases.\r\n\r\nWhat do you think>\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 401199795,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-401199795",
      "created_at": "2018-06-28T23:09:40Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "I spoke to @bojeil-google about this and he brought up a good point - we should only require explicit consent when the user is signing up, which is an issue because we don't distinguish between signups/logins in our UI.\r\n\r\n"
    },
    {
      "id": 401421310,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-401421310",
      "created_at": "2018-06-29T17:28:33Z",
      "updated_at": "2018-06-29T17:32:34Z",
      "author": "Participant 4",
      "body": "@iamyaoxi We're still discussing this internally, we'll get back to you once we decide on a solution. I'd suggest not doing too much work until then. "
    },
    {
      "id": 402054329,
      "url": "https://github.com/firebase/FirebaseUI-Android/issues/1338#issuecomment-402054329",
      "created_at": "2018-07-03T08:22:11Z",
      "updated_at": null,
      "author": "Participant 1",
      "body": "@iamyaoxi @samtstern @lsirac \r\nIndeed, @bojeil-google is right. We should only add the checkbox when the user is signing up. But as you said, the UI doesn't make the difference between signups and logins for social medias and phone. At least, the difference is made for the email way!\r\n\r\nWe could be tempted adding another View for the ToS/PP consent. Such as:\r\n\r\n1. The user uses a social media for example.\r\n2. The Firebase back-end knows if the user has been already registered or not.\r\n3. If not, we show the View for the user consent.\r\n4. If the user doesn't agreed, we cancel the signing-up . \r\n\r\nHowever, I don't know if it's possible. Because, without the user consent, could we send the user data to the Firebase back-end?\r\nIf not, there is any way. Facebook for example doesn't return any data explaining if the user has been already registered or not. It could explain why there is never any checkbox on other knowned websites  when selecting a social media for signing-up. \r\n"
    },

      "updated_at": "2021-05-21T15:48:01Z",
      "author": "Participant 6",
      "body": "+1 - wondering if there are any recommended workarounds in the meantime?  Am considering setting a Firebase custom claim, and showing an additional pop-up after login if absent, but it seems a bit heavy.\r\n\r\n[edit: in case anyone finds it useful, what I did in the end was store on my server a flag representing whether or not the user has accepted the T&Cs; fetch it immediately after login, and if they haven't, then show a second pop-up after the log-in dialog, asking the user to accept the terms., and then after they accept the terms, ping the server again to store the result.]"
